items.followUp: Draw and label a chloroplast, showing its double membrane, grana, lamellae and stroma.

rubric.how: Award for stating that a chloroplast has a double membrane, or for identifying both the outer and inner membranes.

rubric.why: Identifies the fluid interior of the chloroplast.
rubric.how: Award for naming the stroma and identifying it as the fluid interior.

rubric.why: Describes the thylakoids arranged in stacks called grana.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that thylakoids are arranged in stacks called grana.
Award for stating that grana are connected by intergranal lamellae.

rubric.why: Checks that the diagram shows and labels the main chloroplast structures.
rubric.how: Award for a chloroplast diagram showing an oval outline, both membranes, grana, stroma and connecting lamellae, with these structures labelled.

modelAnswer: A chloroplast is surrounded by a double membrane: an outer membrane and an inner membrane.
The interior contains a fluid called stroma.
Within the stroma are flattened membrane sacs called thylakoids, arranged in stacks called grana.
Grana are connected to one another by intergranal lamellae.
Diagram: draw an oval chloroplast with a double outline; show several stacks of discs (grana) inside, connected by lamellae, and label the outer membrane, inner membrane, stroma, granum and lamellae.

items.followUp: Compare the structures and functions of arteries and capillaries.

rubric.why: States the direction in which arteries and veins carry blood.
rubric.how: Award for stating that arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry blood towards the heart.

rubric.why: Compares the wall structure of arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award for describing artery walls as thick, muscular and elastic, and vein walls as thinner and less elastic.

rubric.why: Compares the lumen size of the two vessel types.
rubric.how: Award for stating that arteries have a narrower lumen and veins have a wider lumen.

rubric.why: Describes the role of valves and the difference between the vessels.
rubric.how: Award for stating that veins have valves to prevent backflow, or that veins have valves while arteries generally do not.

rubric.why: Compares the pressure of blood flowing through arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award for stating that blood pressure is higher in arteries and lower in veins.

modelAnswer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood towards the heart.
Arteries have thick, muscular, elastic walls; veins have thinner, less elastic walls.
Arteries have a narrower lumen; veins have a wider lumen.
Veins contain valves to prevent the backflow of blood; arteries generally do not have valves.
Blood flows through arteries at higher pressure, while blood in veins is at lower pressure.
